tools.name: run_task
tools.title: Run a website task
tools.description: Carry out a task on a website from a plain-English goal: navigate, click, type, fill in forms and read the outcome, in a real browser. Returns the outcome and, when result_schema is given, the data in that shape. If the task is still going when the call returns, the reply has status "running" and a task_id: call get_task with it. Each call starts a fresh browser session with no saved logins.

goal.description: What to accomplish, with every detail needed to finish it, e.g. "Find the cheapest direct flight from Boston to Denver on March 3 and return the airline, times and price".

start_url.description: Page to open first (http or https). Omit to let the task find its own way.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape of the data to return, for example {"type":"object","properties":{"price":{"type":"number"}},"required":["price"]}. Omit it for a free-form answer.

effort.description: How much capability to spend. Default medium; raise it for hard pages, lower it for simple ones.

max_cost_usd.description: Stop once the task has spent this many US dollars.

max_steps.description: Stop after this many steps. Default 30.

secrets.description: Names of private values the task may type (passwords, one-time codes). Each value is read from NODEMANTIS_SECRET_<NAME> in this server's environment; refer to one in the goal as <secret:NAME>.

use_proxy.description: Route the browser through the proxy configured in this server's environment. Default false.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window while the task runs. Default false unless the server was started with --headed.

tools.name: retrieve_data
tools.title: Read data from a page
tools.description: Open one page and read data from it without changing anything on it. Returns the data, shaped by result_schema when given. Use run_task instead when getting to the data takes clicking, typing or several pages. If reading is still going when the call returns, the reply has status "running" and a task_id: call get_task with it.

url.description: The page to read (http or https).

prompt.description: What to read from the page, e.g. "every listing with its title, price and link".

result_schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape of the data to return, for example {"type":"object","properties":{"price":{"type":"number"}},"required":["price"]}. Omit it for a free-form answer.

effort.description: How much capability to spend. Default medium; raise it for hard pages, lower it for simple ones.

use_proxy.description: Route the browser through the proxy configured in this server's environment. Default false.

show_browser.description: Show the browser window while the task runs. Default false unless the server was started with --headed.

tools.name: get_task
tools.title: Check a task
tools.description: Wait for a task started by run_task or retrieve_data and return its status, latest progress and, once finished, its result. Returns as soon as the task finishes, or after wait_seconds with status "running" (call again). Tasks are kept for an hour after they finish and are lost when this server restarts.

task_id.description: The task_id returned by run_task or retrieve_data.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the task to finish before answering. 0 answers immediately.

tools.name: cancel_task
tools.title: Cancel a task
tools.description: Stop a running task and close its browser. A task that already finished is left unchanged.

task_id.description: The task_id returned by run_task or retrieve_data.
